symbols.intro: This guide briefly explains what the marks on the wheel are; it is not an interpretation. Hover over a symbol on the wheel (press and hold on touch screens) to see its name and exact degree.

body.sun: The Sun's position in the zodiac at the moment of birth. The Sun travels round the zodiac in about one year (~1° per day).
body.moon: The Moon's position. It is the fastest-moving body: about 12–15° per day, so the birth time noticeably affects the Moon's degree.
body.mercury: The planet closest to the Sun. Seen from Earth, it never moves more than ~28° from the Sun.
body.venus: Seen from Earth, it never moves more than ~47° from the Sun.
body.mars: Travels round the zodiac in about 2 years (687 days).
body.jupiter: Travels round the zodiac in about 12 years.
body.saturn: Travels round the zodiac in about 29.5 years; the most distant of the planets known since antiquity.
body.uranus: Travels round the zodiac in about 84 years.
body.neptune: Travels round the zodiac in about 165 years.
body.pluto: Travels round the zodiac in about 248 years (its orbit is highly eccentric, so the time it spends in each sign varies).
body.north_node: The point where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic from south to north (a calculated point, not a celestial body).
body.chiron: A small body orbiting between Saturn and Uranus (2060 Chiron); travels round the zodiac in about 50 years.
body.lilith: Black Moon Lilith: the point of the Moon's orbit farthest from Earth (apogee). This system uses the mean calculation.

symbols.fortuneText: A point calculated from the Ascendant, Sun and Moon (not a celestial body). For a day birth the formula is Ascendant + Moon − Sun; for a night birth, Ascendant + Sun − Moon.
symbols.vertexText: The point where the prime vertical (the vertical circle running east–west) crosses the ecliptic on the western side; it depends on the latitude and time of birth.
symbols.ascText: The zodiac degree rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth. In most house systems it is the start of the 1st house.
symbols.dscText: The degree on the western horizon; exactly opposite the Ascendant (180°).
symbols.mcText: The degree where the ecliptic crosses the local meridian (towards the south). In systems such as Placidus and Koch it is the start of the 10th house.
symbols.anglesNote: In the Whole Sign and Equal House systems, house cusps may not coincide with the axes; the Natal wheel shows the true ASC–DSC and MC–IC axes separately with a bold line.
symbols.signsNote: The zodiac is 12 equal 30° segments (tropical zodiac; 0° Aries = vernal equinox point). The sign colour shows its element.
symbols.aspectText: An angle of {deg}° between two points.
symbols.aspectMajor: Major aspect: also drawn in the Basic view.
symbols.aspectMinor: Minor aspect: only in the Professional view, as a dashed line.
symbols.aspectsNote: Line colours show the system's aspect class: blue harmonious, red challenging, grey neutral. Two points in conjunction overlap on the wheel, so the conjunction line may not be visible; all aspects are listed in the Aspects tab. The North–South Node opposition is 180° in every chart by definition, so it is not drawn on the wheel.
symbols.orbText: The difference between the actual angle and the exact aspect value. Example: if two planets are 93° apart, the aspect is a square (90°) with an orb of 3°. The maximum orb at which an aspect counts is set by the calculation source; this screen does not change the orb. In the Professional view, the line gets thicker as the orb gets smaller.
symbols.retroText: Seen from Earth, the planet appears to move backwards through the zodiac. This is an apparent motion; the direction of the planet's orbit does not change.
symbols.degreeText: 1° = 60′ (minutes of arc). Degrees are written in the ephemeris tradition by truncating the minutes: 29°59.9′ → 29°59′ (never rounded up into the next sign). On the wheel's scale each tick is 1°, a medium tick 5° and a long tick 10°.
